At the edge of the town, where the last streetlamp gave up and the fields began, there was a mailbox that nobody owned.

Every morning, it held a letter.

The envelopes were addressed to people who had not been born yet. The handwriting was always different: sometimes careful and slanted, sometimes so hurried the ink seemed to run. The letters smelled of rain, or oranges, or the inside of an old library.

No one knew who put them there. No one knew who carried them away.

Then, one winter morning, Mara found an envelope with her name on it.

Inside was a single sentence:

*When you get there, remember to look back.*

She read it twice. Then she turned toward the road, where the town was waking under a thin sheet of frost, and started walking.
